newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, Primakov to meet on Mideast, Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, Primakov to meet on Mideast, Afghanistan.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov will meet on Wednesday to discuss the situation in Afghanistan and the Middle East, the Kremlin press service said.
The meeting will take place in the Central Clinical Hospital where doctors are preparing the 65-year-old Russian leader for a heart operation, due later this year.

Yeltsin told Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on Tuesday to contact some leaders of the Commonwealth of Independent States to consider a meeting aimed to work out steps to prevent fighting in Afghanistan spilling onto former Soviet territory.
The Kremlin did not make clear when the meeting could take place or who would be invited. It did not specify who would represent Russia.
Moscow's immediate worry appeared to be about its border guards, who are helping to patrol the uneasy frontier between CIS member Tajikistan and Afghanistan.
The border has become an effective front line in the prolonged conflict between the pro-Moscow Tajik government in Dushanbe and Islamic guerrillas based in Afghanistan.

Dozens of Russian troops have died in attacks by rebels, who are often backed by Afghan fighters. Moscow is clearly worried that the successes of the Taleban militia in Afghanistan might worsen the situation.

Moscow, officially a co-sponsor of the Middle East peace process, has been sidelined by its partner, the United States, which organised a meeting between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in Washington on Tuesday.
The summit followed violence last week in the West Bank, Gaza and Jerusalem.

Deputy Foreign Minister Viktor Posuvalyuk told Interfax news agency on Tuesday that Primakov would visit Israel during a Middle East tour in about a month and discuss a possible visit to Moscow by Netanyahu.
